findings.reason: the whole section is invoked to shrink a measured population, and as written its measure cannot distinguish reclaiming 22,350 directories from reclaiming none; it needs a required reduction (or a floor on directories removed) and a stated retention window, so the node must show the count fell.
findings.text: the apply pass can reclaim nothing and still satisfy every criterion: the before/after figures are only *recorded*, and the sole population criterion is "no run directory remains that the report named as reclaimable", which holds vacuously when the report names none. `garbage_collect` skips any directory not in the project's ledger (`gc.py:767`, `if directory.name not in ledgered ... continue`) and the unledgered sweep fails closed, marking every row `withheld`, whenever any registered mount's ledger is unreadable (`routing.py:2009-2017`); the unledgered cutoff is also `now - retention_days`, default 30 days (`routing.py:1986`)`, so a rerun on 10 November reaches only directories untouched for a month. A node can therefore run the pass, watch it remove 0 of the 22,350 directories it exists to reclaim, and report the section met.

findings.reason: the pass is irreversible and destructive over a live shared store, and the control as written cannot go red on the failure that matters, which is deleting a peer's live run rather than failing to delete a dead one.
findings.text: the declared negative control is the report-only pass: "after it, the counts and sizes are unchanged". That shows only that a dry run does not write; it presents no case in which the keep-guard must fire and no mutation that makes it red. Nothing in the done-when puts a live run's directory, or a worktree with uncommitted or unreachable commits, in front of the pass and requires it to be skipped and listed as kept, so a gc that removed one would still satisfy the control.

findings.reason: the deliverable and its measure do not rest on which module walks the population, so correcting the sentence changes the rationale and not the work; it is still worth doing because the next reader will look for the walk where the plan says it is.
findings.text: the justification "Every promotion and the station still walk that population" names two callers that do not exist in the tree: no `reckon/crew/station*.py` and no `reckon/crew/promotion*.py` module references `runs_dir`, `runs_root` or `crew/runs`. The readers that do walk it are `recovery_watch.py:3027` (a file stamp over the runs root), `dispatch_claims.py:1797`, `node.py:915` and `routing.py:1980`.
